iosacl_acl_basic.label: Clear all access lists then install new ones. This method may interrupt access to the firewall if you manage it remotely via IPSEC tunnel. This is the way access lists were generated in older versions of Firewall Builder for IOSACL.

iosacl_acl_substitution.label:
"Safety net" method:

First, create temporary access list to permit connections from the management subnet specified below to the firewall and assign it to outside interface. This temporary ACL helps maintain session between management station and the firewall while access lists are reloaded in case connection comes over IPSEC tunnel. Then clear permanent lists, recreate them and assign to interfaces. This method ensures that remote access to the firewall is maintained without interruption  at a cost of slightly larger configuration.

pf_adaptive_end.tooltip: When reaching this number of state entries, all timeout values become zero, effectively purging all state entries immediately.

pf_adaptive_start.tooltip: When the number of state entries exceeds this value, adaptive scaling begins.

pf_block_policy.tooltip:
The block-policy option sets the default behaviour for the packet block action:

drop      Packet is silently dropped.
return    A TCP RST is returned for blocked TCP packets, an ICMP
             UNREACHABLE is returned for blocked UDP packets, and
             all other packets are silently dropped.

pf_do_timeout_frag.label: seconds before an unassembled fragment is expired

pf_do_timeout_interval.label: interval between purging expired states and fragments

pf_flush_states.label: Flush pf states after reloading rules

pf_icmp_error.tooltip: The state after an ICMP error came back in response to an ICMP packet.

pf_icmp_first.tooltip: The state after the first packet.

pf_limit_frags.tooltip: maximum number of entries in the memory pool used for packet reassembly

pf_limit_src_nodes.tooltip: maximum number of entries in the memory pool used for tracking source IP addresses

pf_limit_states.tooltip: maximum number of entries in the memory pool used for state table entries

pf_limit_table_entries.tooltip: maximum number of addresses that canbe stored in tables

pf_limit_tables.tooltip: maximum number of tables that can exist in the memory simultaneously

pf_modulate_state.label: Modulate state for all stateful rules (applies only to TCP services)

pf_optimization.tooltip: Optimize state timeouts. See man pf.conf for more details.

pf_other_first.tooltip: The state after the first packet.

pf_other_multiple.tooltip: The state after the first packet.

pf_other_single.tooltip: The state after the first packet.

pf_scrub_fragm_crop.label: Drop duplicate fragments, do not buffer and reassemble
pf_scrub_fragm_crop.tooltip: Causes duplicate fragments to be dropped and any overlaps to be cropped.  In PF 4.5 and earlier.

pf_scrub_fragm_drop_ovl.label: Drop duplicate and subsequent fragments
pf_scrub_fragm_drop_ovl.tooltip: Similar to 'Drop duplicate fragments' except that all duplicate or overlapping fragments will be dropped as well as any further corresponding fragments.  In PF 4.5 and earlier.

pf_scrub_maxmss.tooltip: Enforces a maximum Maximum Segment Size (MSS) in TCP packet headers.

pf_scrub_minttl.tooltip: Enforces a minimum Time To Live (TTL) in IP packet headers.

pf_scrub_no_df.label: Clear DF bit
pf_scrub_no_df.tooltip: Clears the don't fragment bit from the IP packet header.

pf_scrub_random_id.label: Use random ID
pf_scrub_random_id.tooltip: Replaces the IP identification field of outgoing packets with random values to compensate for operating systems that use predictable values.

pf_scrub_reassemble.label: Buffer and reassemble fragments (default)
pf_scrub_reassemble.tooltip: Buffers incoming packet fragments and reassembles them into a complete packet before passing them to the filter engine. In PF 4.5 and earlier.

pf_set_debug.tooltip:
Set the debug level, which limits the severity of log messages
printed by pf(4).  This should be a keyword from the following
ordered list (highest to lowest): emerg, alert, crit, err,
warning, notice, info, and debug.  The last keyword, debug, must
be quoted.  These keywords correspond to the similar (LOG_)
values specified to the syslog(3) library routine.

pf_state_policy.tooltip:
States can be bound to interfaces or match packets 
on any interface. The latter can be useful in case of 
an assymmetric routing.

pf_tcp_closed.tooltip: The state after one endpoint sends an RST.

pf_tcp_closing.tooltip: The state after the first FIN has been sent.

pf_tcp_finwait.tooltip: The state after both FINs have been exchanged and the connection is closed.

pf_tcp_first.tooltip: The state after the first packet.

pf_tcp_opening.tooltip: The state before the destination host ever sends a packet.

pf_udp_first.tooltip: The state after the first packet.

pf_udp_multiple.tooltip: The state if both hosts have sent packets.

pf_udp_single.tooltip: The state if the source host sends more than one packet but the destination host has never sent one back.

"Safety net" method:

First, create temporary access list to permit connections from the management subnet specified below to the firewall and assign it to outside interface. pix_connection_timewait.label: Force each TCP connection to linger in a shortened TIME&WAIT

pix_emb_limit.label: maximum number of embryonic connections per host
pix_emb_limit.tooltip: Specifies the maximum number of embryonic connections per host. An embryonic connection is a connection request that has not finished the necessary handshake between source and destination. Set a small value for slower systems, and a higher value for faster systems. The default is 0, which means unlimited embryonic connections.

pix_emblem_log_format.label: Use 'EMBLEM' format for syslog messages
pix_emblem_log_format.tooltip: PIX Firewall Version 6.3 introduces support for EMBLEM format, which is required when using the CiscoWorks Resource Manager Essentials (RME) syslog analyzer.

pix_max_conns.label: maximum number of simultaneous TCP and UDP connections
pix_max_conns.tooltip: Specifies the maximum number of simultaneous TCP and UDP connections for the entire subnet. The default is 0, which means unlimited connections. (Idle connections are closed after the idle timeout specified by the timeout conn command.)
